Crayfish Crackdown / Poachers vs Patrols

By: Beth Neale | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
On KwaZulu-Natal’s coastline, a community task force patrols the shore, trying to protect a fragile balance between conservation, crime and survival.  

Unique Selling Point:
Embedded Access to the Coastal Marine Task Force
Rare, frontline access to a fast-growing, community-driven enforcement unit working alongside SAPS and DFFE during active anti-poaching operations.
Powerful Character-Driven Storytelling
Compelling personal journeys within the task force, including members with direct past links to poaching and coastal crime, creating authentic and emotionally layered storytelling.
Time-Critical Filming Window
Filmed during the final days of the closed crayfish season and the February new moon spring tide — a peak period for illegal harvesting and enforcement activity that is difficult to capture at any other time.
Crayfish as More Than a Commodity
The story reframes crayfish as a vital reef species, using underwater footage and ecological context to raise environmental stakes beyond the seafood trade.
High-Impact Visual Storytelling
Night patrols, spring tide rock pools, roadside trade, enforcement busts and underwater reef environments create a visually dynamic and cinematic narrative.


Summary:
Driving along the N2 on the KZN coast, it is not unusual to find roadside vendors selling everything from avocados and golf balls to crayfish — despite the species being strictly protected and currently in closed season.

This story follows the Coastal Marine Task Force (CMTF), a relatively new multi-agency enforcement group working alongside SAPS and the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, as they conduct anti-poaching operations during a period when it is illegal to possess any crayfish. Many of the members previously operated as informal community vigilantes, responding to growing frustration around coastal crime and marine poaching before formal partnerships with authorities were established. The story explores how that transition from community enforcement to recognised operational support has shaped both the task force and the communities they operate within.

Through embedded access, the insert focuses on the people within the task force — who they are, what motivates them, and the risks they face as they attempt to protect marine resources while navigating tensions with coastal communities dependent on ocean harvesting for survival.

Crayfish poaching serves as the narrative thread, allowing the story to move between enforcement operations, harvesting communities, roadside trade and the legal small-scale fishing sector.


Further information:
The title may change based on what the focus will be following the shoot and determined by the bust footage that we manage to get.
